newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile police chief arrested in leftist probe.
newsitem.headline: Chile police chief arrested in leftist probe.

text.p: A Chilean judge ordered the arrest on Wednesday of national police chief Nelson Mery and charged top government officials with obstructing justice in a probe into leftist crimes in the early 1990s, court sources said.
Mery, head of Chile's civilian police force, was accused of hiding evidence relating to the kidnapping in 1991 of Christian Edwards, the son of one of Chile's top newspaper magnates.

Judge Raquel Camposano, who is also investigating the 1991 assassination of rightist senator Jaime Guzman, accused Deputy Regional Development Minster Marcelo Schilling of protecting government informers, who were believed to have links with the leftist guerrillas.
Schilling, who led an intelligence unit during the government of former president Patricio Aylwin, denied the accusations.
"Everything was done within the rule of law ... There has been no obstruction of justice at any moment," said Schilling.
Although both men have been temporarily suspended from their duties, the government said it will not ask them to resign until their cases have been decided by the courts.
Camposano also brought charges against another five government officials and members of the police force.
